# SK0219 — A namespace-qualified reference is not shortened

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

`skala arrange` would drop a namespace qualifier, or a `global::`, that the reference does not need under `skala_prefer_qualified_reference = false`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Formatting |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

A qualifier tells the reader that the short name would have meant something else. Where it would not — `new System.Text.StringBuilder()` beside `using System.Text;` — the qualifier is noise, and an AI-written file carries it in every position. The rule binds the shortened name at the reference's own position and rewrites only when it reaches the same type, so a shadowed or ambiguous name keeps its qualifier.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
using System.Text;

var builder = new System.Text.StringBuilder();
```

Write:

```csharp
using System.Text;

var builder = new StringBuilder();
```

## When it does not fire

Never adds a using: a name whose namespace is not imported stays qualified. Never shortens part-way (`RegularExpressions.Regex` is never written) and never uses an alias. Documentation `cref`s, using and namespace declarations, extern aliases, explicit interface specifiers, comments inside the name and formatter-off regions are left alone. A `global::` whose name cannot lose its namespace loses only the `global::`. A using the shortened name now binds through is kept even if it was unused when the pass began.

## Configuration

- `skala_prefer_qualified_reference`
